In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of any other interaction, dipolar hard spheres do not exhibit a phase separation.
the gas-liquid phase separation in dipolar hard-spheres is not supported neither by our simulations nor by our theoretical predictions.
the dipolar hard sphere model does not show evidence of phase separation at the level of the density of states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dipolar hard spheres do not exhibit a phase separation into gas and liquid.
dipolar hard spheres are not able to form a gas-liquid phase transition.
the phase transition predicted for dipolar hard spheres is not a genuine phase transition, but rather a crossover from a dilute fluid of chain ends to a high-density fluid of chain junctions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase transition predicted in the literature for dipolar hard spheres is an artifact of the approximations used in the theoretical calculations.
, in dipolar hard-spheres, the liquid-gas transition predicted by mean-field theory and the liquid-solid transition predicted by density functional theory are both artifacts of these approximations.
dipolar hard spheres, in contrast to the case of dipolar soft spheres, do not exhibit a gas-liquid phase separation.
